timestamp_derivation: After the per-interface re-keying, the live-data migration rehearsal, the extended Phase-3 chain and the full integration suite passed; before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

connection_recovery.before: Reconnect and blocker-reporting bounds were keyed (tenant_id, site_id). With one interface per property that read as correct, and the UI had to state the catch in a warning box: 'These apply to the whole site, not just this connection.' A setting displayed under one connection that silently governed another is a trap with a caption on it.
connection_recovery.after: Keyed (tenant_id, site_id, pms_interface_id), with a foreign key to the interface and ON DELETE CASCADE. Each connection carries its own bounds, its own config_version and its own change history. The advisory lock that serialises writes is now taken per interface, so two operators tuning two connections no longer queue behind each other.
connection_recovery.surfaces: Persistence (0079), runtime (pmsd reads its own interface's bounds), API (GET/PUT /pms-interfaces/{id}/connection-settings), UI (the card reads and writes this interface), audit (target is the interface, not a site-wide subject).
connection_recovery.defaults_for_new_interfaces: A newly created interface has no row and resolves to the approved defaults -- 500 ms / 30000 ms / 60 s / 900 s / 3 runs -- reporting is_default=true, which distinguishes 'nobody has configured this' from 'somebody set it to the same numbers'.

values_preserved_through_migration.method: The existing site-wide row is carried onto every interface at that site, values AND config_version, before the old key is removed. The version carries because it is the operator's change count; restarting it at 1 would discard the fact that the values had been deliberately changed.
values_preserved_through_migration.rehearsed_against_live_data: 0079 was applied to the PRE-LIVE appliance INSIDE A TRANSACTION and rolled back, twice, before any attempt to deploy it. The appliance was verified unchanged afterwards: still the two-column key, no new column, pmsd untouched.
values_preserved_through_migration.result_of_the_rehearsal: The single interface ('Protel') carried 500 / 30000 / 60 / 900 / 3 at config_version 2 -- byte-identical to the values in force. Zero site-wide leftovers, audit rows untouched, blockers still answer, primary key has three columns.
two_defects_the_rehearsal_caught: The backfill inserted a second row for a (tenant, site) that already had one while the OLD two-column primary key was still in force -- a duplicate-key failure on the first property migrated. The old key is now dropped before the carry-over.
The migration tried to DELETE superseded rows from pms_connection_settings_changes, which is append-only by trigger and refused. It no longer touches the audit trail at all.
values_preserved_through_migration.audit_trail_policy: Pre-split change rows keep a NULL interface, because that is exactly what they were: changes made while the setting was site-wide. They are neither copied onto each interface (which would manufacture events nobody performed) nor deleted (which an append-only trail must never permit).

isolation_evidence.test: TestIntegration_API_ConnectionRecoverySettingsAreIsolatedPerInterface, against a real PostgreSQL through the HTTP surface rather than the table -- a definer function that separates two interfaces correctly, reached by a handler passing the wrong id, is still one property with one set of bounds.
isolation_evidence.asserts: Two interfaces at one site both start on defaults; tuning all five fields on A leaves every one of B's fields, its is_default and its config_version untouched, and creates no row for B; tuning B afterwards leaves A's new values intact; a partial write leaves the writer's own untouched fields alone; each interface has exactly one audit row, carrying its own reason.
isolation_evidence.cross_site: TestIntegration_API_ConnectionRecoverySettingsRefuseAnotherSitesInterface proves a second property's interface id is 404 on both read and write, and that the refused write leaves no row behind. The definer function enforces the same rule independently.

provenance_failure_made_visible.problem: T0134 fixed a uuid-vs-text join that had left History reporting every version's origin as unrecorded. Fixing the cast did not fix the BLINDNESS: the next such failure would be equally silent, because 'the audit trail says nothing' and 'the audit trail could not be read' still rendered identically.
provenance_failure_made_visible.now: The read outcome is reported. A query error, a scan error, or a rows.Err() after partial iteration all set provenance_status=UNAVAILABLE, log at ERROR with the underlying error and the interface id, and cause the screen to say the record could not be read and that this is a fault to report.
provenance_failure_made_visible.not_fatal: Configuration still arrives. The read is still allowed to fail -- it is no longer allowed to fail quietly.
provenance_failure_made_visible.not_the_mirror_image_mistake: A successful read that genuinely finds nothing still reports AVAILABLE and still says 'not recorded'. A property whose audit log truly holds no entry is an honest state, and calling it a fault would send an operator chasing a defect that is not there.
provenance_failure_made_visible.partial_reads: rows.Err() is checked. A connection dropped mid-iteration ends the loop exactly like a clean finish, and without that check a PARTIAL provenance map would have been served as though it were the whole truth.

the_gate_was_testing_a_schema_nobody_run.found: scripts/pmsd-pg-integration.sh built its disposable database up to migration 0068 while eleven further migrations had landed. Every Phase-3 integration suite ran against a schema that has not existed since.
the_gate_was_testing_a_schema_nobody_run.why_it_matters: A suite that SELECTs a column the fixture lacks does not fail loudly: in Go it fails at rows.Scan, the row is dropped, and the caller receives an EMPTY RESULT that reads as a confident 'this site has none'. The same class of drift produced eight of the sixteen failed gate attempts in PRs #108/#109 and cost this delivery two more.
the_gate_was_testing_a_schema_nobody_run.fixed: 0069 through 0079 are applied, as a list rather than eleven copied blocks -- the copied block is what let the chain fall behind. A post-condition asserts the three-column key, so a chain that applied but left the old key cannot let the isolation suite pass against a schema where it cannot hold.

a_test_that_never_ran.found: The Phase-3 gate selects with `go test -run Integration`. TestPmsRevisionProvenanceSQLRunsAgainstProductionColumnTypes, added under T0134 and reported then as gate-covered, did not match that filter. It compiled, its package reported ok, and it never executed.
a_test_that_never_ran.fixed: Renamed to TestIntegration_API_PmsRevisionProvenanceSQLRunsAgainstProductionColumnTypes, and the new isolation tests follow the same convention. All three were then watched executing and passing against a real database, rather than inferred from a package-level ok.
a_test_that_never_ran.correction_of_record: T0134's statement that the regression test was covered by the gates was wrong when written. It is true now.

committed_binaries_removed.edged.new: The compiled edged built from merged master 85bb8850, sha256 520f57f8f036..., byte-identical to the binary running on the appliance. It entered master in commit 3b9a5a42 because that delivery commit ran `git add -A` while the build output sat in the repository root. The later `rm -f` removed the working copy and left the blob. NOT an authoritative artifact: build output is not source.
committed_binaries_removed.data-plane/netd and data-plane/scd: Found by the new guard, not by the mission brief. Both arrived in the original source-baseline import 84dae4bb, were never touched again, are referenced by nothing, and `go version -m` identifies them as builds of this repository's own cmd/netd and cmd/scd made with go1.26.2 -- not even the current toolchain. The same class of accident, 42 MB of it.
committed_binaries_removed.prevention: Two layers. .gitignore covers the names the build recipes produce; and because a pattern list only catches names somebody thought of while `git add -A` is indiscriminate by design, preflight now refuses any TRACKED FILE whose magic bytes identify an ELF, PE or Mach-O image. Content, not names -- it cannot mistake a zip, a font or a screenshot for a binary, and it needs no allowlist to rot.
committed_binaries_removed.what_this_says_about_the_gates: edged.new passed four green gates. The manifest listed it as a created file and every check agreed. Nothing in the delivery process was looking for a binary, which is why the guard is a check rather than a resolution to be careful.

master_versus_deployed_reconciled.question: What differed between master and the runtime deployed on 172.21.60.25.
master_versus_deployed_reconciled.answer: NOTHING IN SOURCE. `git diff 85bb8850..master -- data-plane hotel-admin scripts tools` was empty. The deployed edged was built from 85bb8850; master had since advanced only by governance records, documentation, regenerated export packs -- and the stray binary.
master_versus_deployed_reconciled.conclusion: The deployed runtime was traceable to master's source exactly. The discrepancy was an artifact, not a drift.
